useCases.title: A personal AI agent that is always available
useCases.standfirst: Something like OpenClaw or Hermes that answers when you message it, keeps its files and logins, and does not need a terminal to set up. This is the hardest case for this market, because most providers sell a machine, not an assistant.
needs: A machine that is not killed by a default deadline or an idle timer
A way to reach it from a phone or chat app, not just a laptop terminal
A cheap idle state, because most of the day is idle
Somewhere for files and logins to live between sessions
A way back in after the box stops, without rebuilding it

picks.why: The managed-hosting line is the only genuinely one-click personal agent here: $0 to $99.99 a month, a task board, a web terminal, a file browser and a live desktop. If you want your own box instead, the Cloud 4 vCPU / 8 GiB shape is about $10.60 a month with 20 GB of disk.
picks.watch: The Cloud product needs a terminal or an API call, stop loses memory, and disk bills until you delete.

picks.why: Pause keeps the agent's session, the dashboard creates the machine, and the desktop is clickable. Claude Code and Codex are preinstalled, so you can type a request into the box's terminal.
picks.watch: The free plan caps continuous runtime at 8 hours, public URLs have no password, and fork is not the instant copy the homepage implies.

picks.why: The cheapest exact-fit always-on box with a real 50 GB disk: a 2 vCPU / 4 GB machine is $1.62 for 90 hours or $13.14 always on, with seven coding agents preinstalled and no egress bill.
picks.watch: No pause at all, a one-hour default auto-stop, disk deleted 14 days after a stop, and EU-only regions.

picks.why: Measured CPU makes an agent that waits on a model cheap, and secrets never sit inside the box. One click gives you a shell on free hours with no card.
picks.watch: A stopped box still bills storage, there is one US region, and there is no preinstalled agent.

useCases.avoid: Sandboxer, boxd and Lizard are capable machines but assume a terminal for setup. Lizard's stop deletes the disk, and Sandboxer's trial converts into a $20 plan on day eight.

useCases.title: AI-built apps and websites
useCases.standfirst: An agent writes an app, and the app needs to run somewhere with a URL, a process that restarts, and enough disk for dependencies. The machine is now a small production host, which changes what matters.
needs: A public URL, ideally on a domain you control
A process that restarts if it crashes, or a supervisor that does
Docker or a normal Linux stack
Enough disk for dependencies, builds and uploads
A way to preview a change before it replaces the live one

picks.why: Custom domains, raw TCP ports, token-gated previews and a real Linux desktop, with images built from any Dockerfile. The strongest set of hosting primitives in this group.
picks.watch: One region in Virginia, so no EU residency; nothing is reachable until you open a door.

picks.why: Every machine gets an HTTPS name and a proxy per port, custom domains are self-serve, and Docker is preinstalled and running. A fork gives you a second copy for a preview in 100–200 ms.
picks.watch: The public URL has no authentication in front of it, so your app must provide its own; no status page.

picks.why: A full Ubuntu VM with Docker, 51 GB of disk on the small size, and an HTTPS route per port. No egress bill and a 60 fps desktop for checking the result.
picks.watch: No custom domains, the public URL carries HTTPS and WebSockets only, and regions are EU-only.

picks.why: A stable HTTPS address per port that survives stop, resume and resize, plus a public IPv6 and a real Docker daemon. Hosted ports can be public or token-gated.
picks.watch: Custom domains are still on the roadmap, and the default one-hour TTL will stop a forgotten site.

useCases.avoid: Agent 37's default type is a gVisor container that cannot run Docker, so you need its 2.5× VM type. Lizard's stop deletes the disk. InstaBox has no custom domains and no raw TCP inbound.

useCases.title: Separate workspaces for a team or clients
useCases.standfirst: One machine per person or per client, with credentials kept apart and a bill someone can explain. This is where organisation features, secret scoping and spend controls matter more than hourly price.
needs: One machine per person or client, not one shared box
A way to keep credentials apart between clients
Spend visibility, and ideally a hard cap
Fast copies of a standard setup
An audit trail, if a client asks

picks.why: Every account is an organisation with roles, machines are private to their creator by default, snapshots work as golden images, and host-bound secrets keep client keys out of the machines.
picks.watch: No audit log or spend cap on self-serve, and the machine quota is stated as both 50 and 100.

picks.why: Compartments wall off key groups, keys can carry a daily spend limit, secrets are scoped by label or id, and SSO, SCIM and a 400-day audit log are free.
picks.watch: One region, and a per-sandbox cap is a lifetime cap rather than a monthly budget.

picks.why: Workspaces own keys, wallet and instances; teams have admin and user roles; each instance has a budget ceiling; one instance per end user is the documented pattern.
picks.watch: The instance cap counts sleeping and stopped boxes, so 200 clients means 200 live instances, and there is no audit log.

picks.why: Organisations and workspaces with roles, Org Secrets with host scoping, and a monthly spend cap that stops every sandbox when reached.
picks.watch: Audit logs and SSO are Enterprise only, and a paused machine still counts against plan limits.

useCases.avoid: Sandboxer's organisation plans are priced per seat, so five people on the $20 plan pay $100. Lizard has no spending cap at all. Boat publishes no audit log, and its organisation start budget is pooled, so one member can block everyone else's creates.

useCases.title: Browser automation
useCases.standfirst: An agent that drives a browser needs a real Chromium, enough memory to run it alongside the agent, a way to take over when it gets stuck, and an IP that sites will talk to.
needs: A real Chromium, ideally with a desktop you can watch
Enough RAM for a browser plus an agent
A stable way to drive it: CDP, Playwright, or computer-use tools
An egress IP that is not blocked everywhere
A screen you can take over when it gets stuck

picks.why: The default template ships Chromium, a VNC desktop and a computer-use MCP, and a human can take control of the desktop and hand it back to the agent.
picks.watch: All machines share one NAT egress IP, and there is no stealth or residential proxy option.

picks.why: `agent-browser` is preinstalled, there is a Chromium build with anti-bot fingerprinting, and the desktop is a real display you can click.
picks.watch: No GPU, and anti-bot fingerprinting is a browser property, not a residential IP.

picks.why: Chrome is preinstalled and documented with Playwright, Browser Use and a Selenium Grid; integrated agents get screenshot, click and type tools.
picks.watch: Egress shares the node's IP, and there is no stealth option.

picks.why: Chromium over CDP, so Playwright, Puppeteer, browser-use and Stagehand connect directly, plus a Linux desktop with clicks, screenshots and MP4 recording.
picks.watch: No stealth or residential proxy product; one US region.

picks.why: `desktop-camoufox` adds Camoufox, a Firefox build for scraping driven by Playwright — the only anti-detection option in this set.
picks.watch: It runs only in us-east-1, and the desktop has no public VNC port: you need the CLI bridge.

useCases.avoid: Boat has Chrome 151 and a 60 fps desktop but no GPU, and its raw network path is IPv6-first. Agent 37's default container type has no desktop: you need an agent template or the VM type.
